title: Certified genus-2 Kummer heights and regulators
objective: Implement an honest production-capable genus-2 canonical-height, pairing, and regulator engine with exact Kummer arithmetic, bounded diagnostics, caching, differential tests, and benchmarks

oracles: Muller--Stoll exact Kummer identities and repeated-doubling reference
Magma CanonicalHeight and HeightPairing when licensed oracle is available

handoff.summary: Implements exact QQ Mumford serialization, Cassels--Flynn/Mueller Kummer coordinates, direct sparse Flynn quartic duplication, cached certified canonical heights, pairings and regulators. Primitive integral classical quintics use an exact model-specific duplication L1 audit, Stoll root-partition bounds, certified archimedean correction partial sums/tails, and the factorization-free modular-gcd finite correction of Mueller--Stoll Section 14. Tests cover torsion zero, scaling, basis transforms, the full h2!=0 generalized Kummer transform, seeded constructed-divisor differential corpora against Cantor, nontrivial finite gcd content, and genuine Magma V2.18 CanonicalHeight/HeightPairing/regulator values.
risks: Automatic certification and local-correction decomposition require a primitive integral odd quintic with h=0; generalized h remains exact direct Kummer arithmetic but numerical unless a proved caller bound is supplied.
Even-degree transformations, number fields, and genus 3 are deliberately outside this lane.
The finite engine implements the certified factorization-free modular approximation to arbitrary precision, not the optional exact coprime-factor formal logarithm representation.

architecture:check reaches package-graph validation but the new claimed modules exceed the existing hyperelliptic-curves-algorithms lazy byte budget; integration must split or raise that centrally owned manifest budget.
next_steps: Wire canonical_height, height_pairing, regulator, and capability methods into the centrally owned public Jacobian API and package graph.
Add both strict modules to the central pyright configuration and run integration-owned Linux, Windows, macOS, and Wasm suites.
If exact formal finite corrections are useful to researchers, add the optional Bernstein coprime-factor refinement atop the existing modular gcd sequence.
